original_value: High resolution remote sensing (HRRS) images are widely used in many sensitive fields, and their security should be protected thoroughly. Integrity authentication is one of their major security problems, while the traditional techniques cannot fully meet the requirements. In this paper, a perceptual hashing based forensics scheme is proposed for the integrity authentication of a HRRS image. The proposed scheme firstly partitions the HRRS image into grids and adaptively pretreats the grid cells according to the entropy. Secondly, the multi-scale edge features of the grid cells are extracted by the edge chains based on the adaptive strategy. Thirdly, principal component analysis (PCA) is applied on the extracted edge feature to get robust feature, which is then normalized and encrypted with secret key set by the user to receive the perceptual hash sequence. The integrity authentication procedure is achieved via the comparison between the recomputed perceptual hash sequence and the original one. Experimental results have shown that the proposed scheme has good robustness to normal content-preserving manipulations, has good sensitivity to detect local subtle and illegal tampering of the HRRS image, and has the ability to locate the tampering area.

result.paraphrase: High-resolution remote sensing (HRRS) images are widely used in many sensitive areas, so their security must be thoroughly protected. Integrity authentication is a major security challenge, and conventional methods cannot fully satisfy the requirements. This paper proposes a perceptual-hashing-based forensic scheme for HRRS image integrity authentication. First, the HRRS image is divided into grids, and the grid cells are adaptively preprocessed according to entropy. Next, multi-scale edge features are extracted from the grid cells using edge chains under an adaptive strategy. Then principal component analysis (PCA) is applied to the extracted edge features to obtain robust features, which are normalized and encrypted with a user-set secret key to generate the perceptual hash sequence. Integrity authentication is performed by comparing the recomputed perceptual hash sequence with the original one. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme is robust to normal content-preserving manipulations, sensitive to local subtle and illegal tampering of HRRS images, and capable of locating tampered areas.
